metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
repository_links: SUMO - "evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator"
https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12104 - "preprint in the following link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12104"
supplementary_materials: Data on request - "The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request."
metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 - "finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)."

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic video and volume data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data availability statement specifies access is upon request from the corresponding author; no public link or DOI is provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation is configured using SUMO. The road network connects Qingdao and Huangdao. Speed limits are set to 80 km/h in the mainline and 40 km/h at the on-ramp. Driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data to create a simulated environment.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/1 tools named, 4/4 params stated, but exact empirical calibration data is missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed as the observation input of each decision time step.
nodes_process.description: Video frames from the controlled area are zoomed, down-sampled, and converted to position matrices containing vehicle locations and signal states. Three consecutive observations are stacked to form a state matrix to capture vehicle dynamics.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, generic techniques used without naming libraries, but dimensional parameters are explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: A neural network is initialized to approximate the Q-value function and concurrently predict mean speed and queue length. The architecture includes three CNN layers followed by fully connected layers for multitask learning.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, network architecture thoroughly described in figure 7, library not named.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained for ramp metering using deep Q-learning with experience replay and a target network. An epsilon-greedy strategy explores policies, while multitask loss is optimized using the Adam gradient-based algorithm.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, optimizer named but deep learning framework omitted, comprehensive hyperparameter table provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: The trained DRL method is evaluated against a no-control scenario and the PI-ALINEA baseline method over 20 simulation experiments with different random seeds. Traffic speed, travel times, downstream volumes, and queue lengths are measured.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, baseline parameters explicitly given, experiment counts and comparison framework well specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: An ablation study evaluates the importance of spatio-temporal video data. The control area is divided into eight subareas, and information from each subarea is systematically removed to generate perturbed data and assess the impact on travel times.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, experiment logic clear but exact masking mechanism for the perturbed images is not deeply detailed in equations.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Algorithm and network parameters provided, but exact SUMO network files and raw empirical demand data are not openly available, limiting exact reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Line plot of median and interquartile ranges of mainline travel times for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation method detailed and hyperparameters supplied, but unavailable raw empirical traffic inputs prevent direct validation.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times and percentage improvements for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL across 20 distinct simulation runs.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Experiments clearly defined, but depends on closed-source empirical traffic data and unshared SUMO scenario definitions.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Contour heatmaps showing temporal-spatial speed distributions for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualisation logic is clear, but upstream dataset and simulation scripts are omitted.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Plot displaying median and interquartile bounds of queue lengths over time for the evaluated control methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Calculation is straightforward based on stated methods, though limited by closed data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time)
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots with regression lines showing the correlation between the red phase ratio and queue length for PI-ALINEA and DRL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Aggregates are clearly specified, but cannot be regenerated without the base traffic data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time series plots overlaying occupancy percentages and queue lengths to demonstrate correlation differences between PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Inputs and outputs are clearly matched, but unreleased original trajectory data limits exact reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots illustrating downstream traffic volume measured at 5-minute intervals across three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Consistent with stated methods; lacks source simulation inputs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots quantifying changes in travel time performance when visual information from distinct subareas is masked out in perturbation analysis.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methodological steps for perturbation are described, but the underlying data remains closed.
